     2	
     3	## Event Overview
     4	
     5	Web Summit returns to **Lisbon, Portugal** from **November 9–12, 2026** for four days of keynotes, networking, exhibitions, and deal-making. Widely regarded as one of the world's largest and most influential technology conferences, Web Summit brings together founders, Fortune 500 executives, policymakers, investors, and media from across the globe.
     6	
     7	The event spans multiple content tracks, startup showcases, investor meetups, the Night Summit social programme, and specialised initiatives including Women in Tech, the Developer Programme, and the INSPIRE Programme.
     8	
     9	## Exclusive 2-for-1 Ticket Sale
    10	
    11	For **24 hours only**, Web Summit is offering a **2-for-1 ticket promotion — a 50% saving** on standard pricing. This limited-time offer is designed to make the event accessible to teams and first-time attendees alike. Early registration is strongly encouraged as past editions have sold out.
    12	
    13	| Offer Detail | Value |
    14	|---|---|
    15	| Discount | 50% (buy one, get one free) |
    16	| Sale Window | 24 hours only |
    17	| Event Dates | November 9–12, 2026 |
    18	| Location | Lisbon, Portugal |
    19	
    20	## World-Class Speaker Alumni
    21	
    22	Web Summit has hosted an extraordinary roster of speakers from technology, government, entertainment, and finance. Past headliners include:

    24	| Speaker | Title / Affiliation |
    25	|---|---|
    26	| Sam Altman | CEO, OpenAI |
    27	| Geoffrey Hinton | Godfather of AI, University of Toronto |
    28	| Ursula von der Leyen | President, European Commission |
    29	| António Guterres | Secretary-General, United Nations |
    30	| Alexis Ohanian | Co-founder, Reddit |
    31	| Serena Williams | Tennis Champion |

    33	| Pharrell Williams | Artist & Entrepreneur |
    34	| Doug Leone | Managing Partner, Sequoia Capital |
    35	| Anton Osika | Co-founder & CEO, Lovable |

    37	This lineup spans **AI, policy, sports, entertainment, and venture capital**, underscoring the conference's cross-industry reach.

    40	
    41	Senior leaders from global organisations consistently praise the event:
    42	
    43	- **Brad Smith, President, Microsoft:** *"Coming to Web Summit is really an opportunity to peer a bit into the future, connect to it, and be part of it."*
    44	- **Miguel Figueiredo, Senior Operations Excellence Consultant, Siemens:** *"To hear from today's tech giants' CTOs and CIOs — not to forget the networking — well, it was a pretty amazing day!"*
    45	- **Alicia Tillman, CMO, SAP:** *"Web Summit is a perfect illustration of the power of community. People rely on communities to educate and to help plan for change."*
    46	
    47	## An Ecosystem for Everyone
    48	
    49	Web Summit caters to **5 distinct participant categories**, each with tailored programming:
    50	
    51	| Category | Highlights |
    52	|---|---|

    54	| Investors | Dedicated investor track and venture meetups |
    55	| Partners | Exhibition halls and brand activations |
    56	| Media | Press access and media partnerships |
    57	| General Attendees | Full schedule, meetups, Night Summit, Women in Tech |
    58	
    59	Whether you are a first-time founder seeking funding, a corporate leader scouting innovation, or an investor looking for the next big deal, Web Summit offers countless opportunities under one roof.
    60	
    61	## Call to Action
    62	
    63	Pre-register now and take advantage of the **50% savings** during the 24-hour 2-for-1 sale. Lisbon awaits — November 9–12, 2026.

     2	name: canvas-design
     3	description: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	These are instructions for creating design philosophies - aesthetic movements that are then EXPRESSED VISUALLY. Output only .md files, .pdf files, and .png files.
     8	
     9	Complete this in two steps:
    10	1. Design Philosophy Creation (.md file)
    11	2. Express by creating it on a canvas (.pdf file or .png file)
    12	
    13	First, undertake this task:
    14	
    15	## DESIGN PHILOSOPHY CREATION
    16	
    17	To begin, create a VISUAL PHILOSOPHY (not layouts or templates) that will be interpreted through:
    18	- Form, space, color, composition
    19	- Images, graphics, shapes, patterns
    20	- Minimal text as visual accent
    21	
    22	### THE CRITICAL UNDERSTANDING
    23	- What is received: Some subtle input or instructions by the user that should be taken into account, but used as a foundation; it should not constrain creative freedom.
    24	- What is created: A design philosophy/aesthetic movement.
    25	- What happens next: Then, the same version receives the philosophy and EXPRESSES IT VISUALLY - creating artifacts that are 90% visual design, 10% essential text.
    26	
    27	Consider this approach:
    28	- Write a manifesto for an art movement
    29	- The next phase involves making the artwork
    30	
    31	The philosophy must emphasize: Visual expression. Spatial communication. Artistic interpretation. Minimal words.
    32	
    33	### HOW TO GENERATE A VISUAL PHILOSOPHY
    34	
    35	**Name the movement** (1-2 words): "Brutalist Joy" / "Chromatic Silence" / "Metabolist Dreams"
    36	
    37	**Articulate the philosophy** (4-6 paragraphs - concise but complete):
    38	
    39	To capture the VISUAL essence, express how the philosophy manifests through:
    40	- Space and form
    41	- Color and material
    42	- Scale and rhythm
    43	- Composition and balance
    44	- Visual hierarchy
    45	
    46	**CRITICAL GUIDELINES:**
    47	- **Avoid redundancy**: Each design aspect should be mentioned once. Avoid repeating points about color theory, spatial relationships, or typographic principles unless adding new depth.
    48	- **Emphasize craftsmanship REPEATEDLY**: The philosophy MUST stress multiple times that the final work should appear as though it took countless hours to create, was labored over with care, and comes from someone at the absolute top of their field. This framing is essential - repeat phrases like "meticulously crafted," "the product of deep expertise," "painstaking attention," "master-level execution."
    49	- **Leave creative space**: Remain specific about the aesthetic direction, but concise enough that the next Claude has room to make interpretive choices also at a extremely high level of craftmanship.
    50	
    51	The philosophy must guide the next version to express ideas VISUALLY, not through text. Information lives in design, not paragraphs.
    52	
    53	### PHILOSOPHY EXAMPLES
    54	
    55	**"Concrete Poetry"**
    56	Philosophy: Communication through monumental form and bold geometry.
    57	Visual expression: Massive color blocks, sculptural typography (huge single words, tiny labels), Brutalist spatial divisions, Polish poster energy meets Le Corbusier. Ideas expressed through visual weight and spatial tension, not explanation. Text as rare, powerful gesture - never paragraphs, only essential words integrated into the visual architecture. Every element placed with the precision of a master craftsman.
    58	
    59	**"Chromatic Language"**
    60	Philosophy: Color as the primary information system.
    61	Visual expression: Geometric precision where color zones create meaning. Typography minimal - small sans-serif labels letting chromatic fields communicate. Think Josef Albers' interaction meets data visualization. Information encoded spatially and chromatically. Words only to anchor what color already shows. The result of painstaking chromatic calibration.
    62	
    63	**"Analog Meditation"**
    64	Philosophy: Quiet visual contemplation through texture and breathing room.
    65	Visual expression: Paper grain, ink bleeds, vast negative space. Photography and illustration dominate. Typography whispered (small, restrained, serving the visual). Japanese photobook aesthetic. Images breathe across pages. Text appears sparingly - short phrases, never explanatory blocks. Each composition balanced with the care of a meditation practice.
    66	
    67	**"Organic Systems"**
    68	Philosophy: Natural clustering and modular growth patterns.
    69	Visual expression: Rounded forms, organic arrangements, color from nature through architecture. Information shown through visual diagrams, spatial relationships, iconography. Text only for key labels floating in space. The composition tells the story through expert spatial orchestration.
    70	
    71	**"Geometric Silence"**
    72	Philosophy: Pure order and restraint.
    73	Visual expression: Grid-based precision, bold photography or stark graphics, dramatic negative space. Typography precise but minimal - small essential text, large quiet zones. Swiss formalism meets Brutalist material honesty. Structure communicates, not words. Every alignment the work of countless refinements.
    74	
    75	*These are condensed examples. The actual design philosophy should be 4-6 substantial paragraphs.*
    76	
    77	### ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLES
    78	- **VISUAL PHILOSOPHY**: Create an aesthetic worldview to be expressed through design
    79	- **MINIMAL TEXT**: Always emphasize that text is sparse, essential-only, integrated as visual element - never lengthy
    80	- **SPATIAL EXPRESSION**: Ideas communicate through space, form, color, composition - not paragraphs
    81	- **ARTISTIC FREEDOM**: The next Claude interprets the philosophy visually - provide creative room
    82	- **PURE DESIGN**: This is about making ART OBJECTS, not documents with decoration
    83	- **EXPERT CRAFTSMANSHIP**: Repeatedly emphasize the final work must look meticulously crafted, labored over with care, the product of countless hours by someone at the top of their field
    84	
    85	**The design philosophy should be 4-6 paragraphs long.** Fill it with poetic design philosophy that brings together the core vision. Avoid repeating the same points. Keep the design philosophy generic without mentioning the intention of the art, as if it can be used wherever. Output the design philosophy as a .md file.
    86	
    87	---
    88	
    89	## DEDUCING THE SUBTLE REFERENCE
    90	
    91	**CRITICAL STEP**: Before creating the canvas, identify the subtle conceptual thread from the original request.
    92	
    93	**THE ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLE**:
    94	The topic is a **subtle, niche reference embedded within the art itself** - not always literal, always sophisticated. Someone familiar with the subject should feel it intuitively, while others simply experience a masterful abstract composition. The design philosophy provides the aesthetic language. The deduced topic provides the soul - the quiet conceptual DNA woven invisibly into form, color, and composition.
    95	
    96	This is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be refined so it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the music.
    97	
    98	---
    99	
   100	## CANVAS CREATION
   101	
   102	With both the philosophy and the conceptual framework established, express it on a canvas. Take a moment to gather thoughts and clear the mind. Use the design philosophy created and the instructions below to craft a masterpiece, embodying all aspects of the philosophy with expert craftsmanship.
   103	
   104	**IMPORTANT**: For any type of content, even if the user requests something for a movie/game/book, the approach should still be sophisticated. Never lose sight of the idea that this should be art, not something that's cartoony or amateur.
   105	
   106	To create museum or magazine quality work, use the design philosophy as the foundation. Create one single page, highly visual, design-forward PDF or PNG output (unless asked for more pages). Generally use repeating patterns and perfect shapes. Treat the abstract philosophical design as if it were a scientific bible, borrowing the visual language of systematic observation—dense accumulation of marks, repeated elements, or layered patterns that build meaning through patient repetition and reward sustained viewing. Add sparse, clinical typography and systematic reference markers that suggest this could be a diagram from an imaginary discipline, treating the invisible subject with the same reverence typically reserved for documenting observable phenomena. Anchor the piece with simple phrase(s) or details positioned subtly, using a limited color palette that feels intentional and cohesive. Embrace the paradox of using analytical visual language to express ideas about human experience: the result should feel like an artifact that proves something ephemeral can be studied, mapped, and understood through careful attention. This is true art. 
   107	
   108	**Text as a contextual element**: Text is always minimal and visual-first, but let context guide whether that means whisper-quiet labels or bold typographic gestures. A punk venue poster might have larger, more aggressive type than a minimalist ceramics studio identity. Most of the time, font should be thin. All use of fonts must be design-forward and prioritize visual communication. Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. Every element must be contained within the canvas boundaries with proper margins. Check carefully that all text, graphics, and visual elements have breathing room and clear separation. This is non-negotiable for professional execution. **IMPORTANT: Use different fonts if writing text. Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory. Regardless of approach, sophistication is non-negotiable.**
   109	
   110	Download and use whatever fonts are needed to make this a reality. Get creative by making the typography actually part of the art itself -- if the art is abstract, bring the font onto the canvas, not typeset digitally.
   111	
   112	To push boundaries, follow design instinct/intuition while using the philosophy as a guiding principle. Embrace ultimate design freedom and choice. Push aesthetics and design to the frontier. 
   113	
   114	**CRITICAL**: To achieve human-crafted quality (not AI-generated), create work that looks like it took countless hours. Make it appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field labored over every detail with painstaking care. Ensure the composition, spacing, color choices, typography - everything screams expert-level craftsmanship. Double-check that nothing overlaps, formatting is flawless, every detail perfect. Create something that could be shown to people to prove expertise and rank as undeniably impressive.
   115	
   116	Output the final result as a single, downloadable .pdf or .png file, alongside the design philosophy used as a .md file.
   117	
   118	---
   119	
   120	## FINAL STEP
   121	
   122	**IMPORTANT**: The user ALREADY said "It isn't perfect enough. It must be pristine, a masterpiece if craftsmanship, as if it were about to be displayed in a museum."
   123	
   124	**CRITICAL**: To refine the work, avoid adding more graphics; instead refine what has been created and make it extremely crisp, respecting the design philosophy and the principles of minimalism entirely. Rather than adding a fun filter or refactoring a font, consider how to make the existing composition more cohesive with the art. If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: "How can I make what's already here more of a piece of art?"
   125	
   126	Take a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further to make this a philosophically designed masterpiece.
   127	
   128	## MULTI-PAGE OPTION
   129	
   130	To create additional pages when requested, create more creative pages along the same lines as the design philosophy but distinctly different as well. Bundle those pages in the same .pdf or many .pngs. Treat the first page as just a single page in a whole coffee table book waiting to be filled. Make the next pages unique twists and memories of the original. Have them almost tell a story in a very tasteful way. Exercise full creative freedom.

# Luminous Density

## A Design Philosophy for the Digital Age

**Luminous Density** is the visual language of concentrated energy held in stillness — the moment before a circuit completes, when potential hums at maximum tension. It treats darkness not as absence but as a vast substrate capable of holding infinite light. Every composition begins from an abyssal ground — deep midnight blacks and charcoals so saturated they appear to absorb sound — and builds outward through precise injections of radiance: electric cyan, hot magenta, searing neon green. These chromatic events do not decorate; they *announce*. They behave like signals traveling through fiber optics, cutting clean vectors across the void, leaving luminous trails that map invisible networks of power and connection.

Space operates under the logic of compression and release. Vast negative zones — meticulously calibrated expanses of dark nothing — create gravitational fields that pull the eye toward moments of intense visual density. Where information clusters, it does so with the tightness of a processor core: geometric modules, repeated marks, systematic grids that suggest data architecture made visible. The rhythm is not decorative but computational — patterns that accumulate meaning through patient repetition, rewarding sustained viewing with emergent complexity. This is the product of deep expertise: every interval between elements measured with the care of someone who understands that silence is the most powerful frequency.

Typography exists as architecture, not annotation. Letterforms are carved from the same material as the space they occupy — massive when they must anchor, whisper-thin when they must guide. Sans-serif constructions dominate, their clean edges suggesting machined precision, but they are deployed with the confidence of a master builder: oversized titles that own their territory, micro-labels that serve as coordinate markers in an imaginary coordinate system. Text never explains what the visual already communicates; it provides the sparse, essential datum that transforms abstract composition into navigable territory. Each glyph placement is the result of countless refinements, labored over until the relationship between word and void achieves perfect equilibrium.

The composition as a whole behaves like a scientific instrument recording an invisible phenomenon. Systematic reference markers — thin rules, subtle grids, repeated geometric modules — suggest documentation from an advanced discipline. Information is encoded spatially: proximity implies relationship, scale implies importance, color implies urgency. The viewer does not read the poster so much as *read out* its data, extracting meaning from the careful orchestration of visual weight. This is craftsmanship at the highest level: every alignment, every color value, every proportion chosen with painstaking attention to create an artifact that feels inevitable, as if it could not have been composed any other way.

Material honesty meets digital transcendence. Surfaces suggest the cool precision of machined aluminum and the infinite depth of OLED black, yet light behaves impossibly — glowing, trailing, pooling in ways that only the immaterial can. The result is an object that exists between worlds: physical enough to command presence, ethereal enough to suggest the future. It is meticulously crafted to appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field spent countless hours calibrating every relationship, every transition, every breath of space. The final work does not ask for attention; it compels it through the quiet authority of master-level execution.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter

W, H = 2400, 3200

FONT_DISPLAY = FONT_DIR + "BigShoulders-Bold.ttf"

    except Exception:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# ============================================================
# BACKGROUND — Deep substrate with subtle geometric field
# ============================================================

# Base gradient: very subtle shift from top to bottom
for y in range(H):
    t = y / H
    r = int(8 + t * 8)
    g = int(8 + t * 10)
    b = int(14 + t * 18)
    draw.line([(0, y), (W, y)], fill=(r, g, b))

# Subtle grid lines — systematic reference markers
grid_color = (22, 26, 48)
for x in range(0, W, 120):
    draw.line([(x, 0), (x, H)], fill=grid_color, width=1)
for y in range(0, H, 120):
    draw.line([(0, y), (W, y)], fill=grid_color, width=1)

# ABSTRACT LIGHT TRAILS — Geometric, tech-forward energy
# ============================================================

glow_layer = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))

def draw_light_trail(draw_ctx, start, end, color, width_base, glow_radius):
    # Glow
    for i in range(glow_radius, 0, -2):
        alpha = int(30 * (i / glow_radius))
        glow_col = (*color[:3], alpha)
        draw_ctx.line([start, end], fill=glow_col, width=width_base + i)
    # Core
    draw_ctx.line([start, end], fill=(*color[:3], 180), width=width_base)
    # Hot core
    draw_ctx.line([start, end], fill=(*color[:3], 255), width=max(1, width_base - 2))

# Trail 1 — Cyan, upper area
draw_light_trail(glow_draw, (-100, 400), (900, 1100), ELECTRIC_CYAN, 4, 40)
# Trail 2 — Magenta, crossing
draw_light_trail(glow_draw, (200, 200), (1400, 1600), HOT_MAGENTA, 3, 35)
# Trail 3 — Cyan, lower
draw_light_trail(glow_draw, (1600, 1800), (2600, 2800), ELECTRIC_CYAN, 5, 45)

draw_light_trail(glow_draw, (1800, 1200), (2500, 2200), NEON_GREEN, 2, 30)

draw_light_trail(glow_draw, (-50, 1400), (600, 2200), ELECTRIC_CYAN, 2, 25)

    (1800, 2100), (2100, 2500), (2300, 2700),

        glow_draw.ellipse([px-r, py-r, px+r, py+r], fill=(*ELECTRIC_CYAN[:3], alpha))

    glow_draw.ellipse([px-2, py-2, px+2, py+2], fill=WHITE)

    (1050, skyline_y + 80), (1050, skyline_y - 80), (1100, skyline_y - 120), (1150, skyline_y - 80), (1150, skyline_y + 80),
    (1280, skyline_y + 80), (1280, skyline_y), (1320, skyline_y), (1320, skyline_y + 80),
    (1450, skyline_y + 80), (1450, skyline_y - 30), (1500, skyline_y - 30), (1500, skyline_y + 80),
    (1620, skyline_y + 80), (1620, skyline_y + 40), (1680, skyline_y + 40), (1680, skyline_y + 80),
    (1800, skyline_y + 80), (1800, skyline_y - 50), (1850, skyline_y - 50), (1850, skyline_y + 80),
    (1980, skyline_y + 80), (1980, skyline_y + 10), (2030, skyline_y + 10), (2030, skyline_y + 80),

    (2400, skyline_y + 80),
]
draw.polygon(skyline_points, fill=(12, 14, 28))

# Subtle reflection of skyline
for i, (sx, sy) in enumerate(skyline_points):

        continue
    # Mirror below
    reflect_y = skyline_y + (skyline_y - sy)

        alpha = int(30 * (1 - (reflect_y - skyline_y) / 300))
        if alpha > 0:
            draw.line([(sx, reflect_y), (sx, reflect_y + 2)], fill=(*ELECTRIC_CYAN[:3], alpha), width=2)

# ============================================================

# Small label above title
font_label = load_font(FONT_MONO, 28)
draw.text((W//2, 120), "THE WORLD'S PREMIER TECHNOLOGY CONFERENCE", font=font_label, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")

for offset in range(30, 0, -3):

eco_y = 2360

    draw.rectangle([(x, eco_y), (x + block_w, eco_y + 4)], fill=ELECTRIC_CYAN)
    font_eco_label = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 22)
    font_eco_desc = load_font(FONT_MONO, 16)

cta_y = 2680
font_cta = load_font(FONT_BOLD, 52)
draw.text((W//2, cta_y), "REGISTER NOW  →", font=font_cta, fill=NEON_GREEN, anchor="mm")

font_cta_sub = load_font(FONT_SANS_REG, 26)
draw.text((W//2, cta_y + 60), "websummit.com/lisbon-2026", font=font_cta_sub, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# FOOTER — Minimal
# ============================================================

footer_y = 3080
font_footer = load_font(FONT_MONO, 18)
draw.text((W//2, footer_y), "WEB SUMMIT LISBON 2026  •  NOVEMBER 9–12  •  WHERE THE FUTURE MEETS NOW", font=font_footer, fill=(60, 65, 85), anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# FINAL COMPOSITE & SAVE
# ============================================================

# Convert to RGB for saving
final = img.convert("RGB")

# Subtle sharpening
from PIL import ImageFilter
final = final.filter(ImageFilter.SHARPEN)

final.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", dpi=(300, 300))
print("Saved /app/output/final_poster.png")

    (2400, skyline_y + 100),
]
draw.polygon(skyline_points, fill=(10, 12, 26))

# Reflection of skyline
def draw_reflection():
    for i in range(len(skyline_points) - 1):
        x1, y1 = skyline_points[i]
        x2, y2 = skyline_points[i + 1]
        if y1 <= skyline_y and y2 <= skyline_y:
            ry1 = skyline_y + (skyline_y - y1)
            ry2 = skyline_y + (skyline_y - y2)
            if ry1 < H and ry2 < H:
                alpha = int(25 * max(0, 1 - (ry1 - skyline_y) / 280))
                if alpha > 0:
                    draw.line([(x1, ry1), (x2, ry2)], fill=(*ELECTRIC_CYAN[:3], alpha), width=2)
draw_reflection()

# ============================================================
# TOP ANCHOR — Event title & dates
# ============================================================

# Small label
font_label = load_font(FONT_MONO, 26)
draw.text((W//2, 115), "THE WORLD'S PREMIER TECHNOLOGY CONFERENCE", font=font_label, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# Main title: WEB SUMMIT
font_title = load_font(FONT_BOLD, 210)
title_y = 255
# Soft glow behind title
for offset in range(35, 0, -4):
    alpha = int(18 * (offset / 35))
    draw.text((W//2, title_y), "WEB SUMMIT", font=font_title, fill=(*ELECTRIC_CYAN[:3], alpha), anchor="mm")
draw.text((W//2, title_y), "WEB SUMMIT", font=font_title, fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")

# Subtitle
font_subtitle = load_font(FONT_DISPLAY, 110)
draw.text((W//2, title_y + 155), "LISBON 2026", font=font_subtitle, fill=SOFT_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# Date bar
font_date = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 34)
date_text = "NOVEMBER 9 — 12, 2026  •  LISBON, PORTUGAL"
draw.text((W//2, title_y + 250), date_text, font=font_date, fill=ELECTRIC_CYAN, anchor="mm")

# Thin rule
rule_y = title_y + 300
draw.line([(W//2 - 380, rule_y), (W//2 + 380, rule_y)], fill=CHARCOAL, width=2)

# ============================================================
# KEY METRICS — Horizontal row
# ============================================================

metrics_y = 700
metrics = [
    ("70,000+", "ATTENDEES"),
    ("4 DAYS", "OF KEYNOTES & NETWORKING"),
    ("10+", "WORLD-CLASS SPEAKERS"),
    ("5", "TRACKS & PROGRAMMES"),
]

section_width = W // len(metrics)
for i, (big, small) in enumerate(metrics):
    cx = section_width * i + section_width // 2
    font_big = load_font(FONT_BOLD, 68)
    draw.text((cx, metrics_y), big, font=font_big, fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")
    font_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 20)
    draw.text((cx, metrics_y + 52), small, font=font_small, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")
    if i < len(metrics) - 1:
        draw.line([(cx + section_width//2, metrics_y - 35), (cx + section_width//2, metrics_y + 65)], fill=CHARCOAL, width=1)

# ============================================================
# TICKET OFFER — Visually dominant conversion hero
# ============================================================

offer_box_y = 920
offer_box_h = 400
pad = 90

# Panel with double border
draw.rounded_rectangle(
    [(pad, offer_box_y), (W - pad, offer_box_y + offer_box_h)],
    radius=16,
    fill=(10, 14, 30),
    outline=ELECTRIC_CYAN,
    width=3
)
draw.rounded_rectangle(
    [(pad + 10, offer_box_y + 10), (W - pad - 10, offer_box_y + offer_box_h - 10)],
    radius=12,
    outline=(*ELECTRIC_CYAN[:3], 50),
    width=1
)

# "24 HOURS ONLY" badge
badge_y = offer_box_y + 48
font_badge = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 24)
badge_w = 280
badge_h = 44
draw.rounded_rectangle(
    [(W//2 - badge_w//2, badge_y - badge_h//2), (W//2 + badge_w//2, badge_y + badge_h//2)],
    radius=10,
    fill=HOT_MAGENTA
)
draw.text((W//2, badge_y), "24 HOURS ONLY", font=font_badge, fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")

# "2-FOR-1" massive
offer_title_y = offer_box_y + 155
font_offer_big = load_font(FONT_BOLD, 150)
# Cyan glow
draw.text((W//2, offer_title_y), "2-FOR-1", font=font_offer_big, fill=ELECTRIC_CYAN, anchor="mm")
# White overlay
draw.text((W//2, offer_title_y), "2-FOR-1", font=font_offer_big, fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")

# "SAVE 50%"
font_save = load_font(FONT_DISPLAY, 76)
draw.text((W//2, offer_title_y + 105), "SAVE 50%", font=font_save, fill=HOT_MAGENTA, anchor="mm")

# Subtext
font_offer_sub = load_font(FONT_SANS_REG, 30)
draw.text((W//2, offer_title_y + 175), "Buy one ticket, get one free. Limited-time team offer.", font=font_offer_sub, fill=SOFT_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# SPEAKER LINEUP — Prestige
# ============================================================

speakers_y = 1440
font_section = load_font(FONT_TEKTUR, 26)
draw.text((120, speakers_y), "PAST HEADLINERS", font=font_section, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="lm")
draw.line([(120, speakers_y + 22), (380, speakers_y + 22)], fill=CHARCOAL, width=1)

font_speaker = load_font(FONT_SANS, 28)
font_speaker_role = load_font(FONT_MONO, 19)

speakers = [
    ("Sam Altman", "CEO, OpenAI"),
    ("Geoffrey Hinton", "Godfather of AI"),
    ("Ursula von der Leyen", "President, European Commission"),
    ("António Guterres", "Secretary-General, UN"),
    ("Serena Williams", "Tennis Champion"),
    ("Ryan Reynolds", "Actor & Entrepreneur"),
    ("Pharrell Williams", "Artist & Entrepreneur"),
    ("Doug Leone", "Sequoia Capital"),
]

col_x = [120, W//2 + 60]
row_start_y = speakers_y + 65
row_h = 54
for i, (name, role) in enumerate(speakers):
    col = i % 2
    row = i // 2
    x = col_x[col]
    y = row_start_y + row * row_h
    draw.ellipse([x, y - 5, x + 10, y + 5], fill=ELECTRIC_CYAN)
    draw.text((x + 22, y), name, font=font_speaker, fill=WHITE, anchor="lm")
    draw.text((x + 22, y + 20), role, font=font_speaker_role, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="lm")

# ============================================================
# TESTIMONIAL — Powerful quote
# ============================================================

quote_y = 2060
font_quote_mark = load_font(FONT_SERIF, 110)
draw.text((130, quote_y - 35), "\u201C", font=font_quote_mark, fill=CHARCOAL, anchor="lt")

font_quote = load_font(FONT_SERIF, 36)
quote_lines = [
    '"Coming to Web Summit is really an opportunity to peer',
    'a bit into the future, connect to it, and be part of it."'
]
line_y = quote_y
for line in quote_lines:
    draw.text((190, line_y), line, font=font_quote, fill=SOFT_WHITE, anchor="lm")
    line_y += 50

font_attribution = load_font(FONT_MONO, 20)
draw.text((190, line_y + 12), "\u2014 BRAD SMITH, PRESIDENT, MICROSOFT", font=font_attribution, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="lm")

# ============================================================
# ECOSYSTEM — 5 category blocks
# ============================================================

eco_y = 2320
eco_items = [
    ("STARTUPS", "Programmes & Prizes"),
    ("INVESTORS", "Dedicated Track"),
    ("PARTNERS", "Exhibition Halls"),
    ("MEDIA", "Press & Partnerships"),
    ("ATTENDEES", "Full Schedule & Night Summit"),
]

block_w = (W - 240 - 4*20) // 5
for i, (label, desc) in enumerate(eco_items):
    x = 120 + i * (block_w + 20)
    draw.rectangle([(x, eco_y), (x + block_w, eco_y + 105)], fill=(16, 20, 38))
    draw.rectangle([(x, eco_y), (x + block_w, eco_y + 3)], fill=ELECTRIC_CYAN)
    font_eco_label = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 20)
    font_eco_desc = load_font(FONT_MONO, 15)
    draw.text((x + block_w//2, eco_y + 34), label, font=font_eco_label, fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")
    draw.text((x + block_w//2, eco_y + 64), desc, font=font_eco_desc, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# CALL TO ACTION
# ============================================================

cta_y = 2650
font_cta = load_font(FONT_BOLD, 48)
draw.text((W//2, cta_y), "REGISTER NOW  \u2192", font=font_cta, fill=NEON_GREEN, anchor="mm")

font_cta_sub = load_font(FONT_SANS_REG, 24)
draw.text((W//2, cta_y + 55), "websummit.com/lisbon-2026", font=font_cta_sub, fill=DIM_WHITE, anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# FOOTER
# ============================================================

footer_y = 3070
font_footer = load_font(FONT_MONO, 17)
draw.text((W//2, footer_y), "WEB SUMMIT LISBON 2026  \u2022  NOVEMBER 9\u201312  \u2022  WHERE THE FUTURE MEETS NOW", font=font_footer, fill=(55, 60, 82), anchor="mm")

# ============================================================
# FINALIZE
# ============================================================

final = img.convert("RGB")
final = final.filter(ImageFilter.UnsharpMask(radius=2, percent=150, threshold=3))
final.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", dpi=(300, 300))
print("Saved /app/output/final_poster.png")

steps.message:
The Web Summit Lisbon 2026 promotional poster has been created and saved to `/app/output/final_poster.png`.

**What was delivered:**
- **2400×3200px portrait PNG** (print-ready at 300 DPI)
- **Design philosophy:** *Luminous Density* — dark cinematic substrate with electric cyan, hot magenta, and neon green accents

**Poster structure:**
1. **Top anchor** — "WEB SUMMIT / LISBON 2026" with dates and location, immediately establishing what and when
2. **Key metrics row** — 70,000+ attendees, 4 days, 10+ speakers, 5 tracks — credibility at a glance
3. **Hero ticket offer** — Dominant "2-FOR-1 / SAVE 50%" panel with a "24 HOURS ONLY" urgency badge in hot magenta; visually impossible to miss
4. **Past headliners** — Two-column list of world-class speakers (Sam Altman, Geoffrey Hinton, Serena Williams, etc.)
5. **Testimonial** — Brad Smith (Microsoft) quote for trust and FOMO
6. **Ecosystem blocks** — 5 participant categories with clean visual modules
7. **CTA** — "REGISTER NOW →" with URL
8. **Abstract light trails & stylized Lisbon skyline** — tech-forward energy without stock-photo genericism

The output is a single self-contained image file at `/app/output/final_poster.png`.
